name: Buenos Aires
operatingHours: The Subte runs ~5:30 AM–~10:30 PM Mon–Sat and ~8:00 AM–~10:00 PM on Sundays and holidays (last trains leave central stations ~10:00–10:30 PM). No all-night service; trains every 3–8 min by day.
fareInfo: Subte single ride $1,753 ARS from 1 Sept 2026 with a registered SUBE card; unregistered SUBE costs ~$2,541 ARS. Foreign visitors can register a SUBE card online or buy at a kiosk (Subte stations do not sell cards). Buses and suburban trains also use SUBE with their own fares. Fares change often with inflation.

stations: Plaza de los Virreyes - Eva Perón

sights.name: Teatro Colón
sights.note: One of the world's great opera houses, with a seven-tier horseshoe hall and renowned acoustics; visit by guided tour or a performance.
sights.hours: Guided tours daily ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM; performances vary

sights.name: Puerto Madero
sights.note: The redeveloped dockside district of brick warehouses, waterfront restaurants and the white Puente de la Mujer footbridge.

sights.name: La Recoleta Cemetery
sights.note: A labyrinth of marble mausoleums and statues, including Eva Perón's family tomb, laid out like a miniature city.

sights.name: Japanese Garden (Jardín Japonés)
sights.note: A tranquil Japanese landscape garden with koi ponds, a tea house and a cultural centre in Palermo.

sights.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
sights.note: Argentina's national fine-arts museum, with a strong run of European masters and Argentine painting, free to enter.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri 11:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sat–Sun 10:00 AM–8:00 PM, closed Mon; free

sights.name: Palermo Soho
sights.note: A cobbled neighbourhood of boutiques, design shops, cafés and bars centred on Plaza Serrano.
sights.hours: Streets open daily; shops ~11:00 AM–8:00 PM

sights.name: MALBA
sights.note: The leading Latin American modern art museum, with Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera and top Argentine artists in a glass-fronted building.
sights.hours: Thu–Mon 12:00 PM–8:00 PM (Wed to 9:00 PM), closed Tue

sights.name: Bosques de Palermo
sights.note: Buenos Aires's main green lung, with rose gardens, lakes and cycle paths crossing a wide park in the north of the city.

sights.name: Caminito
sights.note: A short, brightly painted pedestrian street in La Boca, famous for tango dancers and colourful tin houses.
sights.hours: Open daily; shops and artists ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: San Telmo Sunday Fair (Plaza Dorrego)
sights.note: A Sunday market of antiques, crafts and street tango around the cobbled plaza in San Telmo.

sights.name: La Bombonera (Boca Juniors Stadium)
sights.note: Boca Juniors' stadium, a steep, concrete bowl with a museum and a guided stadium tour.
sights.hours: Museum and tours daily ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed on match days

sights.name: Casa Rosada
sights.note: The pink presidential palace on Plaza de Mayo, open on weekends for free guided visits.
sights.hours: Free tours on Sat–Sun ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM (by registration)

sights.name: Catedral Metropolitana
sights.note: The neoclassical cathedral on Plaza de Mayo where General San Martín's mausoleum stands.

sights.name: El Zanjón de Granados
sights.note: A guided underground tour through restored 18th-century tunnels and cellars beneath a San Telmo townhouse.

sights.name: Mercado de San Telmo
sights.note: A 1897 iron-and-glass market hall mixing antiques stalls, produce and small food counters.

sights.name: Floralis Genérica
sights.note: A giant stainless-steel and aluminium flower sculpture that once opened and closed its petals with the sun.

railStations.name: Retiro
railStations.note: Buenos Aires's main northern rail hub: Mitre, Belgrano Norte and San Martín commuter lines, with Subte Lines C and E at the door (Retiro station).
railStations.hours: Commuter trains ~4:30 AM–midnight; Subte C/E ~5:30 AM–10:30 PM.

railStations.name: Constitución
railStations.note: Southern hub for the Roca line (commuter and long-distance services toward Mar del Plata and the coast, which run on their own timetables), with Subte Line C at the station.
railStations.hours: Commuter trains ~4:30 AM–midnight; Subte C ~5:30 AM–10:30 PM.

airports.name: Ministro Pistarini International Airport (Ezeiza)
airports.transitNote: ~35 km south-west. No rail or Subte link. Use the Tienda León shuttle bus to Retiro (~45–60 min), an official remis/taxi (~45–60 min) or a public bus. Not on the Subte map.
airports.hours: Airport open 24 hours; shuttle buses and taxis run all night.

airports.name: Jorge Newbery Airport (Aeroparque)
airports.transitNote: In the city beside the river, mostly domestic and regional flights. No Subte link: take a taxi or bus (lines 33, 37, 45) to Plaza Italia (Line D) or Retiro; ~15–25 min to Palermo.
airports.hours: Open ~5:00 AM–midnight; taxis and buses meet flights.
